column2: Space Invaders, the 1978 cabinet: black glass with coloured cellophane bands tinting the sprites by height. Each numeral is a formation of little invaders (crabs, squids, octopi) marching in lock-step, legs flipping on every beat of the four-note thump, the formation stepping and dropping. A cannon below fires, shields crumble. Minute turn: the old formation is shot down evenly and a new wave marches into the new digit after :00. Hour: the mothership run, the time still reading.

A beehive frame, flat wax, amber and honey colours. Each numeral is a run of hexagonal cells full of honey, worked by bees (bold stripes, clear wings) that crawl along the strokes and waggle-dance on the beat while the honey glints. Minute turn: bees uncap and empty the old digit's cells while new comb is drawn and filled into the new digit after :00. Hour: the swarm lifts off and resettles, the time still reading.

A ramen counter in flat Japanese menu illustration: broth, steam lines, a narutomaki swirl, nori. Each numeral is one long hand-pulled noodle laid in the broth, wobbling and sliding along its own length on the beat as chopsticks stir. Minute turn: chopsticks lift and slurp the old noodle away and a fresh one is dropped in and settles into the new digit after :00. Hour: the chef's big pull, the time still reading.

A brick wall under a railway bridge, flat spray-paint art. Each numeral is a wildstyle piece (arrows, fat outlines, flat fill bands, drips), worked by a crew whose cans hiss on the beat: fresh highlights flash, drips run, outlines get re-sprayed. Minute turn: the buff roller paints over the old digit and a can sprays the new one, outline first, after :00. Hour: a train rolls past carrying a whole-car piece, the time still reading.

A 1930s Busby Berkeley aquacade seen from above: tiled pool, flat turquoise water, caustic ripples. Each numeral is a line of synchronised swimmers in bright caps, arms sweeping and legs kicking white splash on the beat, with a kaleidoscope flourish that flowers out and back every ~12 s. Minute turn: the old digit's swimmers swim into the new formation. Hour: the grand finale, the time still reading.

A stadium card stunt: the numerals are drawn by a stand full of fans, each holding up a coloured card (a few pixels per seat), heads and arms showing between rows. On every beat a ripple of card flips runs through the digits; every ~12 s the stand does a Mexican wave with the time still held up. Minute turn: a flip front runs through the section from the old picture to the new. Hour: the big stunt, the time still reading.

Cats in flat Japanese woodblock style. Each numeral is a cat (or two) curled, stretched, sitting or perched into its shape: the 0 curled round, the 1 sitting tall, the 7 lying along a ledge. Tails swish, ears flick and eyes blink on the beat; a yarn ball rolls and gets batted. Minute turn: the old cat stretches, yawns and walks off while the new one jumps in and settles into the new digit after :00. Hour: a chase, the time still reading.

A Showa-era pachinko playfield, flat printed board, brass pins. Steel balls (flat discs with one glint) rain from the top, ricochet through the pin field and pile into pockets shaped as the numerals, so each digit is a heap of jostling balls; the jackpot lights chase on every beat. Minute turn: the old pocket's gate opens and its balls pour out while the new digit fills after :00. Hour: fever mode, the time still reading.
